Hi Sara / Nimbus team —

Attached is a short proposal (Nimbus_Negotiation_Proposal_v1.pdf) and an accompanying channel margin workback (channel_margin_workback.xlsx). High level: we propose a 2-line billing model for simplicity —

- Monthly base: per-seat subscription (invoices monthly). Seats are pooled; unused seats are credited at the end of each month as a pro-rated credit applied to the next invoice. Credits are based on active seat-days (example in the PDF).
- Usage line: metered inference credits billed daily and invoiced monthly. Usage above the included threshold is charged at the listed per-credit rate.

Reseller commission: we recommend a 12% gross commission to ClearWave on total contract value (base + usage). For Nimbus, given volume expectations, we're prepared to tier commission to preserve net revenue: 14% for first year and step down to 10% at renewal if committed consumption targets are hit (see the workback). That preserves a ~5–8% net uplift to Redwood after marketplace/listing fees and taxes.

Questions we had from reading your note:
1) Do you prefer credits flow as a line-item negative on the next invoice, or as an up-front reservation refund? We can do either but the accounting impact differs.
2) Are you comfortable with a single reseller commission waterfall (ClearWave receives commission, they handle local resale taxes) or do you need a two-step (ClearWave then sub-resellers)?

Next steps: if comfortable, we'll prepare a DocuSign with the package and the SOW. Tim (ClearWave) — copied — can you confirm expected payout cadence?

Thanks,
Camila

Subject: INTERNAL: pricing options and net rev scenarios for Nimbus bundle

Camila / Marcus — quick internal note before we respond with a final offer: I modeled three options in channel_margin_workback.xlsx (tabs A/B/C). Short summary:

- Option A (Conservative): 10% reseller commission, seat credit as next-invoice credit. Lists remain higher; net rev ~88% of list after marketplace fees.
- Option B (Balanced): 12% reseller commission + 6% early-adopter credit for year 1 (applied to usage). Net rev ~81–83% of list depending on usage mix.
- Option C (Aggressive): 16% reseller commission with larger included usage bucket and seat-commit smoothing. Net rev ~76% but accelerates adoption and reduces churn risk.

Marcus: based on your channel targets, what's the minimum gross commission ClearWave expects to participate on a co-sell? My model assumes 12% as our starting point. Also note tax handling: if commission is invoiced to ClearWave as a reseller fee vs. passed through as a discount, our accounting treatment changes — we should align with finance on recognition.

I'll prepare a redline-friendly SOW that makes the seat-credit mechanism explicit (active seat-days) and includes an example invoice. Recommend we lead with Option B and keep Option A as fallback.

— Ben

Subject: Final proposal: blended seat + metered credits (Option B suggested)

Sara — thanks for the clarity. Per internal alignment (Ben/Marcus copied) we recommend Option B as the best balance for Nimbus:

- Model: Monthly base (seats) + metered inference credits line.
- Seat crediting: unused seat-days converted to pro-rated credit applied to the next invoice. Example: a 30-day month, seat unused for 10 days => credit = 10/30 * seat price. This is called out in the attached SOW.
- Pricing & early-adopter: Year 1 6% usage credit applied monthly (applies only to usage over included threshold) if signed by 2028-06-30.
- Reseller commission: 12% gross commission to ClearWave on total ARR for year 1; step-down to 10% at renewal if consumption commitments are met. ClearWave confirms they will be single-step reseller (no sub-resellers) for this contract.

Attachments: Nimbus_Negotiation_Proposal_v1.pdf (redlines welcomed), channel_margin_workback.xlsx (detailed math), MAP_and_SOW_draft.docx (SOW with seat-credit clause).
